name: Whisper ASR Webservice
description: ahmetoner/openai-whisper-asr-webservice — a FastAPI/uvicorn HTTP wrapper around OpenAI Whisper (and Faster-Whisper/WhisperX backends) exposing speech-to-text over a REST API with an auto-generated Swagger UI. Root path 307-redirects to /docs. The two signature endpoints are POST /asr (transcribe/translate) and POST /detect-language. No built-in authentication in the upstream image.
auth_notes: No authentication of any kind in the upstream ahmetoner image. The FastAPI app is constructed with no dependency-based auth; /asr and /detect-language accept arbitrary multipart audio uploads from any client. Operators are expected to front the container with a reverse proxy (nginx/caddy/traefik basic-auth or an API-gateway) but the image ships none and most public deployments expose port 9000 raw. There is no auth-enabling env var in the app itself; the only gate is whatever the operator bolts on externally. HuggingFace token is only relevant if a diarization-capable backend (whisperx) is swapped in.

shodan_dorks.rationale: FastAPI app title is projectMetadata['Name'].title().replace('-',' ') = 'Whisper Asr Webservice', rendered verbatim in the Swagger UI <title> and openapi.json info block. Direct vendor-unique name match. Caveat: root / issues a 307 redirect to /docs, so this string appears only when Shodan followed the redirect / crawled /docs — records that only captured the bare 307 will miss it (coverage gap, not a false positive).

shodan_dorks.query: port:9000 http.title:"Whisper Asr Webservice - Swagger UI"
shodan_dorks.rationale: Exact Swagger UI page title when Shodan reaches /docs. Extremely low FP; the ' - Swagger UI' suffix is FastAPI's default and the prefix is the app name.

Co-occurrence of the two signature route paths in the rendered openapi.json / Swagger schema body. /detect-language is nearly unique to this project; combined with /asr on 9000 it eliminates generic OpenAI-compat and other whisper wrappers. Highest-precision body dork.
detect-language endpoint name plus swagger asset reference; catches deployments where the openapi schema is inlined but the app-title string was minified/altered by a fork.

The app passes version=projectMetadata['Version'] into the FastAPI info block, so the running package version (e.g. 1.9.x) is disclosed in openapi.json / Swagger info. Use for CVE/version-targeted scoping of the fleet.

known_vulns: No built-in auth — unauthenticated POST /asr accepts arbitrary audio and returns transcripts to any caller (compute theft + audio PII disclosure)
Unrestricted file upload: no MIME-type validation or file-size cap by default — multi-GB uploads exhaust CPU/GPU and host disk (DoS)
ffmpeg invocation on uploaded media — historical decode/parsing memory-safety surface (feed malicious container/codec streams) reachable pre-transcription
FastAPI /docs, /openapi.json enabled by default — full schema + parameter disclosure aids automated enumeration and version fingerprinting
No rate limiting — GPU/CPU compute-exhaustion attack is trivially automated at operator cost
Backend/model version and library stack (openai-whisper / faster-whisper / whisperx) disclosed via openapi info block, narrowing exploit selection
risk_notes: Primary attack vectors: (1) Compute theft — an open /asr on a GPU host is free transcription at operator cost ($0.006-0.024/GPU-min on rental fabric), automatable with any HTTP client and impossible to attribute back. (2) Audio PII exfiltration — medical dictation, legal/financial calls, and meeting audio transcribed with no auth, no consent gate, and no audit logging in the default config; the returned transcript is the PII. (3) Language/metadata harvesting via /detect-language reveals operator use-cases. (4) DoS / cost-bombing via unbounded uploads and no rate limit. (5) Model/stack version disclosure via openapi.json feeds targeted CVE selection against the underlying whisper/ffmpeg stack. Because root redirects to /docs, these hosts are visually obvious in a browser and trivially triaged at scale.
deployment_notes: Overwhelmingly Docker: onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice, tag :latest (CPU) or :latest-gpu (CUDA). Port 9000/tcp is the hard default in the image and rarely changed. Runs uvicorn (Server: uvicorn header). Common on Vast.ai / RunPod / Lambda GPU rentals and on self-hosted homelab boxes; frequently exposed raw with no proxy. Distinct from whisperx (slug: whisperx, port 8000/8080) and from faster-whisper-server (port 8000, OpenAI /v1/* compat) — this project is the /asr + /detect-language shaped API, not the OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/transcriptions shape, though newer releases can proxy multiple backends. The backend engine (openai-whisper vs faster-whisper vs whisperx) is selectable via ASR_ENGINE env var and disclosed in the openapi info.
